description: Evolve a messy, hard-to-read Python transaction summarizer into clean, performant, Martin-Fowler-approved code. The function takes a list of transaction dicts (with 'type', 'amount', 'customer', 'category' keys) and returns a summary dict with 'total', 'count', 'avg', 'top_customers', 'categories', and 'has_whale'. It must pass all correctness tests while maximizing readability and performance.

optimization_strategies.name: clean_naming
optimization_strategies.description: Replace all cryptic variable names with descriptive, intention-revealing names. Function name should describe what it does.
optimization_strategies.hint: Think about what Martin Fowler would name these variables. 'd' -> 'transactions', 't' -> 'total_revenue', 'zz' -> 'customer_totals'. The function name should be a verb phrase like 'summarize_transactions'.

optimization_strategies.name: pythonic_idioms
optimization_strategies.description: Replace anti-patterns with Pythonic constructs: direct iteration, defaultdict, Counter, comprehensions.
optimization_strategies.hint: Replace range(len(x)) with direct iteration. Use collections.defaultdict or Counter instead of manual dict building. Use dict/list comprehensions where they improve clarity.

optimization_strategies.name: extract_helpers
optimization_strategies.description: Extract logical sub-operations into well-named helper functions to reduce complexity.
optimization_strategies.hint: Consider extracting: _aggregate_by_customer(), _aggregate_by_category(), _find_top_customers(). Each helper should do one thing well. Keep the main function as a clear orchestrator.

optimization_strategies.name: add_documentation
optimization_strategies.description: Add a proper docstring with parameter descriptions, return type, and brief examples.
optimization_strategies.hint: Use Google or NumPy docstring style. Document the expected input format and output structure. Add type hints to the function signature.

optimization_strategies.name: optimize_performance
optimization_strategies.description: Eliminate redundant iterations, use efficient data structures, reduce algorithmic complexity.
optimization_strategies.hint: The baseline does O(n*c) work for categories due to linear scans inside loops. A single pass with dicts can do O(n). Use sorted() with key= instead of manual sorting.

constraints: The function MUST accept a list of dicts with keys: 'type', 'amount', 'customer', 'category'
The function MUST return a dict with keys: 'total', 'count', 'avg', 'top_customers', 'categories', 'has_whale'
'top_customers' must be a list of (name, amount) tuples, sorted descending by amount, limited to 5
'categories' must be a dict mapping category name to {'revenue': float, 'orders': int, 'avg': float}
'has_whale' must be True if any customer spent more than 10000
The function must handle empty input lists gracefully
Refunds subtract from total and from customer totals, but do NOT create category entries
Only standard library imports allowed (collections, typing, dataclasses, etc.)
